# A set is open in the topology generated by a basis iff it is a union of basis elements

Let $X$ be a topological space and let $\mathcal{B}$ be a basis of its topology. Here a *basis* of the topology of $X$ is a collection $\mathcal{B}$ of subsets of $X$ that covers $X$, such that for all $B_1, B_2 \in \mathcal{B}$ and $x \in B_1 \cap B_2$ some $B_3 \in \mathcal{B}$ satisfies $x \in B_3 \subseteq B_1 \cap B_2$, and such that the topology of $X$ is the topology generated by $\mathcal{B}$. Then a subset $U \subseteq X$ is open if and only if $U$ is the union of some subcollection of $\mathcal{B}$; the empty subcollection, whose union is $\varnothing$, is allowed.

## Sources

- James R. Munkres, Topology, 2nd ed., Prentice Hall, 2000.
- The mathlib Community, *mathlib4* at revision 56a005855ea17e0b0958f73ec801ae140b0a1679, for a basis of a topology as a collection that covers the space, satisfies the intersection condition and generates the given topology: `TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis`, https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/56a005855ea17e0b0958f73ec801ae140b0a1679/Mathlib/Topology/Bases.lean#L73-L79.
